title: The switch statement: menus and fixed choices

visuals.title: Day of the week: every case has a break
Membership perks: no break means fall-through

goal: After this you can write a switch menu with case, break and default, explain fall-through, and know when to use if-else-if instead.
warmup: At the canteen counter there is a menu board: press 1 for biryani, 2 for karahi, 3 for tea. The cashier does not check ranges or do any maths. She just looks at your number and goes straight to that line of the menu. If your number is not on the board she says 'sorry, not available'. A switch works like this menu board: one value, direct jump to the matching choice.
definition: A switch statement picks one block of code by comparing ONE expression with fixed values called cases. The expression must be an integer type or a char (not double, not string). Each case value must be a constant and different from the others. switch tests equality only, so it cannot test ranges like marks >= 50.
howItWorks: Press Play, or change the value in the visualizer. The computer evaluates the expression once, finds the case with the same value, and jumps to it. It then runs every statement from there until it meets break or reaches the closing brace. That is why break is important: without it the computer keeps running into the next case. This is called fall-through. If no case matches, the default block runs. default is optional and is usually written last.

pseudocode: CASE a, A, e, E, i, I, o, O, u, U: PRINT "Vowel"

explanation.text: The ch value is compared with each case label.
Capital and small letters are different characters, so both need a case.
Cases with no statements and no break fall through to the next one. That is useful here: all ten labels share one action.
The shared action for every vowel.
break stops the computer from running default.
Any other letter is a consonant (we assume the user types a letter).

variations.way: switch with a break in every case
variations.when: Normal menus: exactly one action per choice
You want a message when no case matches
Ranges, decimals, strings, or complex conditions

mistakes.wrong: switch (n) { case 1: cout << "A"; case 2: cout << "B"; case 3: cout << "C"; }
mistakes.right: switch (n) { case 1: cout << "A"; break; case 2: cout << "B"; break; case 3: cout << "C"; }
mistakes.error: No compiler error. Without break the program falls through: with n = 2 it prints BC instead of B.

mistakes.wrong:
double q = 2;
switch (q) { case 1: cout << "A"; break; }
mistakes.right:
int q = 2;
switch (q) { case 1: cout << "A"; break; }

mistakes.error: the value of 'marks' is not usable in a constant expression (switch cannot test ranges; use if)

mistakes.wrong: switch (n) { case 1: cout << "A"; break; case 1: cout << "B"; break; }
mistakes.right: switch (n) { case 1: cout << "A"; break; case 2: cout << "B"; break; }

examTips: switch works only with int and char expressions. double, float and string are not allowed.
Always write break at the end of every case unless you want fall-through on purpose.
default runs when no case matches. It is optional but good practice.
case values must be constants and must be unique. 'a' and 'A' are different.
switch checks equality only. Use if-else-if for ranges such as marks >= 50.
romanSummary: switch ek variable ki exact value dekh kar sahi case chunta hai.
switch mein sirf int ya char chalta hai, float ya string nahi.
Har case ke baad break lagana zaroori hai, warna agle case mein fall through ho jata hai.
Jab koi case match na kare to default chalta hai.
Ranges jaise marks >= 50 switch se check nahi hoti, un ke liye if-else-if use karo.

practice.prompt: Which type can NOT be used as the switch expression?
practice.explanation: switch works with integer types and char. double values are not exact, so they are not allowed.

practice.hint: There is no break after case 2.
practice.explanation: The computer jumps to case 2 and prints B. With no break it falls into case 3 and prints C, then break stops it. default is never reached.

practice.hint: case 'B' has no statements of its own.
practice.explanation: case 'B' matches and falls through to the statements of case 'C', which print Pass, then break ends the switch.

practice.hint: What stops the computer from running into the next case?
practice.explanation: Add break after case 1, otherwise execution falls through into case 2.

practice.prompt: Fill in the blank: the block that runs when no case matches is called ______.
practice.hint: It is the last label of a switch.
practice.explanation: default handles every value that does not match any case.

practice.prompt: Which problem is best solved with if-else-if instead of switch?
options: Printing a grade from marks ranges
Printing a day name from 1 to 7
practice.answer: Printing a grade from marks ranges
practice.explanation: Marks ranges like 85 to 100 need comparison operators, so an if-else-if ladder is the right tool.

practice.prompt: Canteen menu: 1 = Biryani Rs 250, 2 = Karahi Rs 800, 3 = Tea Rs 50. Read the choice, print Price: Rs followed by the amount, and print Invalid choice for anything else. Use a switch.
practice.hint: One case per menu number, each ending with break.
practice.explanation: A switch on the integer choice with three cases and a default for invalid values.

quiz.prompt: What does break do inside a switch?
quiz.explanation: break jumps to the first statement after the closing brace of the switch.

quiz.prompt: When does the default block run?
options: Only when there is a break
quiz.explanation: default handles every value not listed as a case.

quiz.prompt: What happens if you forget break at the end of a case?
options: Execution continues into the next case
quiz.answer: Execution continues into the next case
quiz.explanation: Without break the computer runs the next case statements too, until it meets a break or the end.

quiz.prompt: Which of these is a valid switch case label?
quiz.hint: Cases are constant whole values or characters.
quiz.explanation: A char constant is valid. Ranges, decimals and strings are not allowed.

quiz.prompt: n = 1. What does switch (n) { case 1: cout << "X"; case 2: cout << "Y"; break; case 3: cout << "Z"; } print?
quiz.explanation: case 1 prints X, falls into case 2 which prints Y, and break stops there.
